title: 2026 GRADE 10 HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP MS T2
text:
ANSWERS
SECTION A: [30 MARKS]
1. (a) Category: Written sources / Archival sources. (1 mk)
(b) Selection: Letters, Diaries, Government reports, Photographs (Any two - 2 mks).
(c) Distinction:
 Primary: First-hand accounts/original materials from the time of the event (e.g., an eye-witness). (1.5
 mks)
 Tertiary: Collections or indexes that summarize primary and secondary sources (e.g., Bibliographies,
 Almanacs). (1.5 mks)
2. (a) Route M: Semites (1 mk)
 (b) Social Effects: Intermarriage, Cultural exchange (language/naming), Spread of religious beliefs,
 Population redistribution. (Any three - 3 mks).
 (c) Reasons: Search for pasture/water, Internal conflicts, Population pressure, Outbreak of diseases/pests.
 (Any two - 2 mks).
3. (a) Energy Source: Coal. (1 mk)
 (b) Impact on Economy: Growth of E-commerce, Mobile banking (M-Pesa), Remote work/Job creation in
 tech, Precision agriculture. (Any three - 3 mks).
 (c) Environmental Challenges: Air pollution (CO2 emissions), Deforestation, Global warming, Water
 contamination. (Any two - 2 mks).
4. (a) Organization: The Commonwealth. (1 mk)
 (b) Principles: Sovereignty, Equality, Rule of Law, Democracy. (Any two - 2 mks).
 (c) Challenges: Economic disparities among members, Political instability in some states, Climate change
 threats to small island members, Regional trade blocks competing with Commonwealth ties. (Any three - 3
 mks).
5. (a) Pillar: Public Participation / Civic Engagement. (1 mk)
 (b) Categorization: (i) Social Resource. (ii) Economic Resource. (2 mks)
 • (c) Measures: Reporting vandalism, Attending public budget hearings, Participating in peaceful audits,
 Educating others on resource sustainability. (Any three - 3 mks).
SECTION B: [50 MARKS]
6. (a) Event: The Berlin Conference (1884–1885). (1 mk)
 (b) Methods: Signing of Treaties, Military conquest (Force), Use of Chartered Companies (IBEACO). (3 mks)
 c) Economic Reasons: Need for raw materials, Market for finished goods, Investment of surplus capital,
 Control of strategic trade routes. (4 mks)
 (d) Players: Britain, Germany, France, Portugal, Belgium, Italy (Any four - 4 mks).
7. (a) Leader: Julius Nyerere. (1 mk)
 (b) Factors: Return of WWII veterans, Spread of Pan-Africanism, Impact of the Cold War, Influence of the
 Labor Party in Britain. (Any three - 3 mks).
 (c) Political Effects: Weakened the prestige of colonial masters, Veterans learned military skills used in
 resistance, Increased demand for self-determination, Encouraged the formation of political parties. (4 mks)
 (d) Lessons from Sankara: Integrity/Anti-corruption, Self-reliance (Pan-Africanism), Women's
 empowerment, Environmental conservation (tree planting). (4 mks).
8. (a) Abolitionist: Olaudah Equiano (1 mk)
 (b) Distinction: Slavery is legal ownership of a person; Servitude is a state of being a subject or forced labor
 often under contract or social debt. (2 mks)
 (c) Modern Forms: Human trafficking, Debt bondage, Forced child labor, Organ harvesting trade. (Any three
 - 3 mks).
 (d) Roles of Missionaries: Preached equality of all humans, Established "Freed Slave Centers" (e.g.,
 Freretown), Provided education/vocational skills to former slaves, Lobbied European governments to ban the
 trade. (4 mks).
9. (a) Document: The Constitution of Kenya 2010. (1 mk)
 (b) Challenges: Negative ethnicity, Corruption, Post-election violence, Political assassinations. (Any three - 3
 mks).
 (c) Prevention of Conflict: Bill of Rights protection, Devolution of resources, Independence of the Judiciary,
 Chapter 6 on Leadership and Integrity. (4 mks).
10. (a) Era: Digital Age / Internet Age. (1 mk)
 (b) Milestones: Invention of the Printing Press, Invention of the Telegraph, Discovery of the World Wide Web
 (Internet), Smartphones/AI integration. (Any three - 3 mks).
 (c) Ethical Challenges: Data privacy/Identity theft, Spread of "Fake News" (misinformation), Cyberbullying,
 Digital divide (inequality in access). (4 mks).
